archetype.name: Pocket Passer (late-career, short-area)
archetype.definition: A 42-year-old who wins with timing and placement from the pocket on short and middle throws, rarely leaves it, and now gives back much of what he gains through sacks and a fading deep ball.

report.headline: Volume and touchdowns cover a sack-heavy, below-average efficiency profile
report.take:
Rodgers' box score and his efficiency tell two different stories. He ranks 16th in passing yards per game at 242.7 and 7th in touchdowns with 13, and the Steelers are 5-2. Per dropback he sits 34th of 45 at -0.089 EPA, against a league average of 0.04. Much of the volume comes from the setup: Mike McCarthy's offense passes 4.2 points more often than the situation predicts, 3rd-most in the league, even though its run game ranks 2nd in rush EPA and its passing game 28th. Rodgers gets plenty of attempts, and he isn't turning them into much.

The throws themselves are not the main problem. On 0-9 yard throws he posts +0.193 EPA with a +6.5 CPOE and 9 of his 13 touchdowns, and over the middle he is at +0.57 EPA on 59 attempts. Both his under-10 and 10-plus depth groups add up to positive EPA. The sacks are what drag the dropback total down to -28. He is pressured on only 18.8% of dropbacks (13th of 38), yet 35.8% of those pressures become sacks (30th of 38). He has 22 sacks, and 14 of them came on third down, where his EPA is -0.29 and the offense converts just 32%. With 4 scrambles all year, this is a quarterback who holds the ball waiting for something to open rather than throwing it away or running.

The career shows this is not a new slump. His pressure-to-sack rate was 0.315 in 2024 and 0.341 last year, near the bottom of the league both times. His EPA per play has sat around 0.04 to 0.06 since 2022, a long way from the 0.36 of 2020. What changed this year is the shape of his game: time to throw is up 0.15 seconds, aggressiveness is up, and he is averaging 35.1 more yards per game than last season. The bad-throw rate actually improved. The added downfield intent has not paid off, though. On 20-plus air yards he completes 19.4% with a -16 CPOE. That is the deep ball of a 42-year-old, and it rarely connects.

The last five games are better: +0.019 EPA per dropback and 12 touchdowns, which excludes the 3-20 loss at New England (-21.4 EPA). The Tampa Bay game is a warning, though. Against a top-3 defense that blitzed him 21 times he completed 33 of 49 with a +5.6 CPOE and still finished at -13.5 EPA on five sacks and a 3.6-yard intended air depth. When a good defense takes away the middle and gets home, there is little left.

strengths.title: Short and middle accuracy
strengths.body: Rodgers is still precise inside 10 yards and between the numbers: +0.193 EPA with a +6.5 CPOE on short throws and +0.57 EPA over the middle. This is timing, anticipation and placement, and it has held up across his career even as his arm has aged. It should hold up the rest of the year and is the base of the offense.

strengths.title: Pass-heavy volume drives production
strengths.body: The Steelers pass well above expectation, so Rodgers gets close to 38 attempts a game whatever his efficiency. That is why his yardage and touchdown ranks sit far above his EPA rank. As long as McCarthy keeps this approach, the volume is reliable.

strengths.title: Red-zone touchdown conversion
strengths.body: Nine of his touchdowns came in the red zone, and his 4.9% TD rate is above the league's 4.5%. The red-zone EPA is still negative (-0.21) because of five sacks inside the 20. The touchdown count comes from quick, short-area throws near the goal line and should mostly hold, though not at a rate that rises above average.

concerns.title: Pressures turn into sacks
concerns.body: He doesn't face much pressure, but when he does it becomes a sack far more often than for most of the league, and he scrambles only rarely. This is a multi-year trait, ranking near the bottom in 2024 and 2025 as well, so it is part of who he is now rather than bad luck. It is the main reason his dropback EPA is negative while his charted throws are positive.

concerns.title: Third downs stall drives
concerns.body: Facing an average of 7.6 yards to go, he has been sacked 14 times on 75 third-down dropbacks, completes 49.2%, and posts -0.29 EPA. Long third downs force him to hold the ball for routes past the sticks, which is exactly where his sack problem and weak deep game meet. Unless early downs get him into shorter distances, this persists.

concerns.title: The deep ball isn't there
concerns.body: He is more aggressive than last year, but 20-plus air-yard throws are completing at 19.4% with a -16 CPOE and two interceptions. The three deep touchdowns keep the total from being a disaster. At his age, this looks like arm decline rather than noise, and the shots mostly cost drives.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung from -21.4 at New England to +8.5 against Cincinnati, and the last five games (+0.019 per dropback) show a recovery from that Week 2 low. A -13.5 showing against Tampa Bay in Week 6 proves the floor is still low against good defenses.

nextGame.headline: Cleveland's pass rush meets his worst habit
nextGame.body:
Cleveland is close to the worst opponent for this profile. The Browns rank 6th in pass EPA allowed, 6th in sack rate and 6th in hit rate, so the pressure that Rodgers turns into sacks will show up. Their stingiest role is the top tight end (-0.16 EPA allowed, 2nd), which hurts Freiermuth's middle-of-the-field targets, where Rodgers does his best work. The first meeting fits the pattern: 299 yards and three touchdowns, but two interceptions, five sacks, a 25.6% bad-throw rate and only +2.4 EPA. The way through is the ground game. Cleveland allows explosive runs more often than any defense (rank 32), Pittsburgh ranks 2nd in rush EPA, and offenses already run more than usual against the Browns. A Steelers lead of the size the Book expects (PIT -3.5, total 39.5) could trim his attempts.

On availability, Pittsburgh's only listed absence is depth receiver Ben Skowronek (12% of snaps), which changes little. Cleveland is without rotational DT Mike Hall Jr. (46% of snaps), which takes some push out of the interior rush. CB Myles Harden (63%) is questionable with a hamstring. If he sits, the outside throws where Rodgers has been below average to both sides get a softer look. The early forecast shows drizzle and gusts near 22 mph, which is worth checking on Sunday but not enough to build on yet.

keyMatchups.title: Browns pass rush vs. slow trigger
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland gets home at a top-6 rate, and Rodgers converts pressure into sacks at a bottom-10 rate. He took five sacks in the first meeting, matching his season high. Whether he gets the ball out on third down decides whether drives survive.

keyMatchups.title: Middle of the field squeezed
keyMatchups.body: His best area is over the middle, and Cleveland has smothered top tight ends. If Freiermuth is taken away, Rodgers has to work outside, where he is negative to both sides.

keyMatchups.title: Run game as release valve
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland leaks explosive runs, and Pittsburgh's ground game is one of the league's best. Leaning on it would shorten third downs and cut the dropbacks where Rodgers gets hurt. It would also cap his passing volume.

nextGame.watch: His third-down sack count. If Cleveland keeps him in third-and-long and gets home, the game turns into another punt-heavy grind.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the steady part. Pittsburgh's pass-first lean and a top-6 defense keep games within one score, so he should keep throwing high-30s attempts with yardage in the 205-255 range and roughly one and a half to two touchdowns a game. Efficiency should settle near where the last five games put it: about league-average-minus, not the -0.089 dragged down by New England. The short-area accuracy is real and has held up across seasons. The sack rate is also real, a trait for three years running, so expect about three a game to keep sinking third downs.

What is likely to slip is the touchdown count on the deep shots. Three deep touchdowns on a 19.4% completion rate is a fragile mix, and the interception risk on those throws hasn't gone away. Age is the other variable: at 42.9, any physical wear would show first in an arm that already isn't reaching downfield.
swingFactors: Protection and ball-out speed on third down
Whether the run game shortens his third-down distances

confidence.note: Seven starts, but the core traits match his last three seasons.
